raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With HiCache on a hybrid sliding-window (SWA) model, prefill admission can accept a host load-back that the SWA pool cannot serve. `alloc_for_extend` then raises and the scheduler dies; every later request fails:

```
alloc_for_extend -> alloc_token_slots: RuntimeError: Out of memory. Try to lower your batch size.
Try to allocate 2318 tokens.
Available full tokens: 7949 (full_available_size=4137 + full_evictable_size_=3812)
Available swa: 2270 (available_size=2270 + component_evictable_size_=0)
```

`PrefillAdder.add_one_req` selects the request while only its device match (`req.last_node`) is pinned. After `init_load_back`, the request's sliding-window lock is anchored at `req.best_match_node`, and that window can cover device-resident SWA past `last_node`. Selection counted that SWA as evictable, and nothing charged it: `swa_host_hit_length` covers only the host-only part of the window.

`add_one_req` already pins `best_match_node` around `memory_budget.prepare_load_back(...)`. `SharedSWAPrefillBudget` (unified memory) implements that hook, but `SWAPrefillBudget`, used by the separate FULL/SWA pools and the Mamba tri-pool, inherits the base no-op. So on the default allocator nothing checks SWA with the window pinned.

Observed with Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it (window 1024) on one RTX 5090, at 28 concurrent multi-turn chat sessions, on a build of `main` from 2026-09-21 (a9871012ac). The admission path involved is unchanged on current `main`, and the unit test below reproduces the same accounting on it. The batch was a 2071-token chunk continuation plus a 247-token request whose prefix sat mostly on host (5286 FULL tokens, 1019 SWA tokens to load):

| step | SWA free | SWA evictable | SWA reserved by batch | remaining SWA |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chunk admitted | 3131 | 508 | 2072 | 1567 |
| load-back selected (needs 1442) | 3131 | 508 | 2072 | 1567 |
| after `init_load_back` | 2112 | 158 | 2072 | 198 |
| after commit | 2112 | 158 | 2495 | -225 |

The load-back allocated the 1019 SWA tokens it was charged for and also locked 350 evictable device SWA tokens (two nodes above the host segment) that it was not charged for.

## Modifications

- `SWAPrefillBudget.prepare_load_back`: run the same SWA check `check_prefill` uses, now with `best_match_node` pinned, so the device SWA the load-back will lock is no longer counted as evictable. An over-committing load-back returns `NO_TOKEN` and is retried in a later round instead of crashing the scheduler.
- `SWAPrefillBudget._swa_fits`: the comparison (`<=` for per-request SWA rings, `<` otherwise), shared by `check_prefill` and `prepare_load_back`.
- FULL needs no re-check: selection already bills every token past the device match as a new allocation.
- Test `TestHiCacheLoadBackSWAWindow` in `test/registered/unit/managers/test_prefill_adder.py` replays the batch above against a tree whose SWA evictable size depends on which nodes are locked:
  - The over-committing load-back must not be admitted, the admitted batch must fit free + evictable SWA, and no lock may leak. This fails on `main`, where the load-back is admitted with 2318 tokens to allocate from 2270.
  - With enough SWA the same load-back is still admitted and leaves only its own locks.

This changes default behavior: an over-committing load-back now waits instead of crashing the scheduler. A load-back that fits is admitted exactly as before, so there is no option to turn it off.

Known limitation: the re-check runs with both admission pins held, the device-match pin on `last_node` and the load-back pin on `best_match_node`. After admission only the `best_match_node` window stays locked, so when the two windows do not overlap, the re-check also excludes up to one window that the request will release. With ordinary SWA pools that slack is negligible, but on a pool of about three windows or less a load-back can be refused every round even on an idle server, where `main` would admit it and run. The same applies to a request that cannot fit the SWA pool even when empty: `check_prefill` shrinks its chunk using the unpinned figure, and the re-check can refuse the shrunk chunk every round. `SharedSWAPrefillBudget.prepare_load_back` behaves the same way.

Two alternatives were considered:
- Run selection itself under the `best_match_node` pin, as the re-check does. This has the same double pin. It also counts FULL KV that is resident behind host-only SWA twice, since `total_tokens` already bills it.
- When the re-check refuses, fall back to recomputing the host part instead of waiting, through the existing `_select_prefill_admission(host_hit_length=0, ...)` path. That removes the stall, but under SWA pressure it trades a short wait for recomputing the whole host hit. I kept the smaller change; happy to switch if reviewers prefer the fallback.

Related: #42703 keeps a cached prompt reusable by a short re-match on SWA models; it came from the same Gemma-4 chat load. Independent of this PR.

## Accuracy Tests

Not applicable: admission accounting only, no kernel or model change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No reproduction on a public model: the crash depends on which SWA nodes the device match leaves behind, and a 15-minute load did not hit it on `main`. The unit test above is the reproduction. The same load checks that the re-check costs nothing when it does not fire.

Setup: `google/gemma-4-E4B-it` on one RTX 5090, `--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-size 8 --hicache-write-policy write_through --max-total-tokens 60000 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.35` (21K-token SWA pool). Load: 40 multi-turn sessions taking turns through 24 concurrent workers for 15 minutes, greedy `/generate` with `input_ids`. Each session starts from a 3000-token prompt and adds its 150-token reply and 200 new tokens per turn, resetting at 6000 tokens.

| build | requests completed | prefix tokens reused | failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 2873 | 20.2% | 0 |
| this PR | 2873 | 20.3% | 0 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (no user-facing change)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

Unit tests (pytest on a GPU host, rebased on f2f0be731c): `test_prefill_adder.py`, `test_schedule_policy.py` and `test_prefill_memory_budget.py` pass (73). Before the rebase, `test/registered/unit/managers` and `test/registered/unit/mem_cache` matched `main` plus the two new cases; the one failure there (`test_mm_process_config.py::TestStreamOrderedMmFeaturePool::test_consumer_slot_uses_global_tp_rank`) also fails on `main` in the same environment.

@@ -15,8 +15,8 @@
 The scheduler supplies token demand and its chunk/decode limits. These objects
 account for admitted but not yet allocated work and query live cache capacity:
 locking a prefix or preempting a request must affect the next admission check.
-Selection checks do not mutate cache state. Shared-pool load preparation
-realizes the selected reservation before a host transfer pins device rows.
+Selection checks do not mutate cache state. Load preparation runs once the
+host match is pinned: separate pools re-check it, shared pools realize it.
 """
 
 from typing import Optional
@@ -85,7 +85,7 @@ def prepare_load_back(
         swa_host_hit_length: int,
         chunk_limit: int | None,
     ) -> bool:
-        """Prepare pools whose admission depends on movable shared space."""
+        """Re-check or realize admission with the load-back's host match pinned."""
         return True
 
     def _available_and_evictable(self):
@@ -217,6 +217,33 @@ def swa_never_fits(self, extend_input_len, max_new_tokens, **kwargs):
             else needed >= self.allocator.size_swa
         )
 
+    def _swa_fits(self, needed: int) -> bool:
+        return (
+            needed <= self.remaining_swa
+            if self.req_ring
+            else needed < self.remaining_swa
+        )
+
+    def prepare_load_back(
+        self,
+        *,
+        full_tokens: int,
+        extend_input_len: int,
+        max_new_tokens: int,
+        swa_host_hit_length: int,
+        chunk_limit: int | None,
+    ) -> bool:
+        # Selection pinned only the device match; best_match_node's window, now
+        # pinned too, can hold device SWA past it that selection counted as free.
+        return self._swa_fits(
+            self.swa_tokens(
+                self.ceil_paged_tokens(extend_input_len),
+                max_new_tokens,
+                chunk_limit=chunk_limit,
+                swa_host_hit_length=swa_host_hit_length,
+            )
+        )
+
     def _chunk_cap(self, max_new_tokens, swa_host_hit_length=0):
         # Only the sliding window stays locked between chunks, so a smaller
         # chunk can bound the transient SWA footprint of a longer prompt.
@@ -245,12 +272,7 @@ def check_prefill(
             chunk_limit=chunk_limit,
             swa_host_hit_length=swa_host_hit_length,
         )
-        fits = (
-            needed <= self.remaining_swa
-            if self.req_ring
-            else needed < self.remaining_swa
-        )
-        if fits:
+        if self._swa_fits(needed):
             return True, chunk_limit
         # Only permanent shortfalls may shrink a chunk. Transient pressure waits
         # so a new prefill does not consume running decodes' window headroom.

@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 import unittest
+from collections import Counter
 from types import SimpleNamespace
 from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
 
@@ -30,6 +31,7 @@
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.radix_cache import RadixCache
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_cache.component_type import ComponentType
 from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_memory_pool import init_unified_swa_pools
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.unified_radix_cache import UnifiedRadixCache
 from sglang.srt.runtime_context import get_context
 from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs, set_global_server_args_for_scheduler
 from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
@@ -1789,5 +1791,208 @@ def test_swa_never_fits_is_gated_by_pool_capacity(self):
         )
 
 
+class _WindowLockTree:
+    """SWA lock accounting of a unified radix tree, reduced to what prefill
+    admission reads: locking a node protects the device SWA segments inside
+    that node's sliding window, and a HiCache load-back allocates the host-only
+    part of the window and locks the window from `best_match_node`."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *, swa_available, windows, other_swa_evictable):
+        self.swa_available = swa_available
+        # node -> {segment: tokens} of device SWA its window lock protects.
+        self.windows = windows
+        self.other_swa_evictable = other_swa_evictable
+        self.locks = Counter()
+
+    def swa_evictable_size(self):
+        locked = {
+            segment
+            for node, count in self.locks.items()
+            if count
+            for segment in self.windows.get(node, {})
+        }
+        segments = {
+            segment: tokens
+            for window in self.windows.values()
+            for segment, tokens in window.items()
+        }
+        return self.other_swa_evictable + sum(
+            tokens for segment, tokens in segments.items() if segment not in locked
+        )
+
+    def inc_lock_ref(self, node, skip_lock_components=()):
+        self.locks[node] += 1
+        return IncLockRefResult(node_id=node)
+
+    def dec_lock_ref(self, node, params=None, skip_swa=False):
+        assert self.locks[node] > 0, f"unbalanced release of {node}"
+        self.locks[node] -= 1
+        return DecLockRefResult()
+
+    def lock(self, node, skip_lock_components=()):
+        return TreeLock(node, self.inc_lock_ref(node).to_dec_params())
+
+    def unlock(self, lock):
+        if lock is not None:
+            self.dec_lock_ref(lock.node, lock.receipt)
+
+    def init_load_back(self, params):
+        self.swa_available -= params.req.swa_host_hit_length
+        # The in-flight load holds its own lock until the H2D ack.
+        self.inc_lock_ref(params.best_match_node)
+        return params.host_hit_length, params.best_match_node
+
+
+class TestHiCacheLoadBackSWAWindow(CustomTestCase):
+    """A HiCache load-back must not be admitted on device SWA that its window lock
+    (from best_match_node, past the device match) takes; replays a real crash."""
+
+    WINDOW = 1024
+    DEVICE_PREFIX = 13
+    HOST_HIT = 5286
+    SWA_HOST_HIT = 1019
+    EXTEND = 247
+    CHUNK = 2071
+    WINDOW_DEVICE_SWA = 350
+    OTHER_SWA_EVICTABLE = 158
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"))
+
+    def _build(self, *, swa_available):
+        tree = _WindowLockTree(
+            swa_available=swa_available,
+            windows={"best_match": {"device_window": self.WINDOW_DEVICE_SWA}},
+            other_swa_evictable=self.OTHER_SWA_EVICTABLE,
+        )
+        # The load-back pin applies to the unified radix tree only.
+        tree_cache = MagicMock(spec=UnifiedRadixCache)
+        tree_cache.disable = False
+        tree_cache.buffer_pipeline = None
+        tree_cache.linker = None
+        tree_cache.sliding_window_size = self.WINDOW
+        tree_cache.supports_mamba.return_value = False
+        tree_cache.full_evictable_size.return_value = 0
+        tree_cache.swa_evictable_size.side_effect = tree.swa_evictable_size
+        tree_cache.inc_lock_ref.side_effect = tree.inc_lock_ref
+        tree_cache.dec_lock_ref.side_effect = tree.dec_lock_ref
+        tree_cache.lock.side_effect = tree.lock
+        tree_cache.unlock.side_effect = tree.unlock
+        tree_cache.inc_host_lock_ref.return_value = IncLockRefResult()
+        tree_cache.dec_host_lock_ref.return_value = DecLockRefResult()
+        tree_cache.init_load_back.side_effect = tree.init_load_back
+        tree_cache.tree_core = MagicMock()
+        tree_cache.tree_core.build_hicache_transfers.return_value = [
+            SimpleNamespace(host_indices=torch.arange(self.HOST_HIT))
+        ]
+
+        allocator = MagicMock()
+        allocator.page_size = 1
+        allocator.size_swa = 42985
+        allocator.full_available_size.return_value = 100_000
+        allocator.available_size.return_value = 100_000
+        allocator.swa_available_size.side_effect = lambda: tree.swa_available
+        allocator.create_prefill_budget.side_effect = lambda tree_cache, **kwargs: (
+            SWAPrefillBudget(allocator, tree_cache, **kwargs)
+        )
+        running_batch = MagicMock()
+        running_batch.reqs = []
+        adder = PrefillAdder(
+            page_size=1,
+            tree_cache=tree_cache,
+            token_to_kv_pool_allocator=allocator,
+            running_batch=running_batch,
+            new_token_ratio=1.0,
+            rem_input_tokens=16384,
+            rem_chunk_tokens=4096,
+        )
+        return tree, adder
+
+    def _req(self, rid, *, prefix_len, fill_len, max_new_tokens, last_node):
+        req = MagicMock(spec=Req)
+        req.rid = rid
+        req.cache_request_handle = CacheRequestHandle(rid, 0)
+        req.priority = 0
+        req.prefix_len = prefix_len
+        # A spec=Req mock gets a per-instance class; derive extend_len like Req.
+        type(req).extend_len = Req.extend_len
+        req.extend_end = None
+        req.full_untruncated_fill_ids = list(range(fill_len))
+        req.output_ids = []
+        req.sampling_params = SimpleNamespace(
+            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, ignore_eos=False
+        )
+        req.retracted_stain = False
+        req.host_hit_length = 0
+        req.swa_host_hit_length = 0
+        req.storage_hit_length = 0
+        req.storage_hit_start = None
+        req.host_hit_is_storage = False
+        req.host_loaded_length = 0
+        req.materialized_host_hit_len.return_value = 0
+        req.fulfilled_storage_hit_len.return_value = 0
+        req.needs_host_load_back.return_value = False
+        req.last_node = last_node
+        req.best_match_node = last_node
+        req.kv = SimpleNamespace(cache_protected_len=prefix_len, holds_mamba=False)
+        return req
+
+    def _admit_batch(self, *, swa_available):
+        tree, adder = self._build(swa_available=swa_available)
+        prefix = 4108
+        chunked = self._req(
+            "chunked",
+            prefix_len=prefix,
+            fill_len=prefix + self.CHUNK,
+            max_new_tokens=204,
+            last_node="chunk_tail",
+        )
+        self.assertIsNone(adder.add_chunked_req(chunked))
+
+        loaded = self._req(
+            "load-back",
+            prefix_len=self.DEVICE_PREFIX,
+            fill_len=self.DEVICE_PREFIX + self.HOST_HIT + self.EXTEND,
+            max_new_tokens=175,
+            last_node="device_prefix",
+        )
+        loaded.host_hit_length = self.HOST_HIT
+        loaded.swa_host_hit_length = self.SWA_HOST_HIT
+        loaded.needs_host_load_back.return_value = True
+        loaded.best_match_node = "best_match"
+        verdict = adder.add_one_req(
+            loaded, has_chunked_req=False, truncation_align_size=None
+        )
+        return tree, adder, loaded, verdict
+
+    def _assert_allocatable(self, tree, adder):
+        # alloc_for_extend takes every admitted extend from free + evictable SWA.
+        demand = sum(req.extend_len for req in adder.can_run_list)
+        self.assertLessEqual(demand, tree.swa_available + tree.swa_evictable_size())
+
+    def test_load_back_waits_when_its_window_lock_overcommits_swa(self):
+        tree, adder, loaded, verdict = self._admit_batch(swa_available=3131)
+        self.assertNotIn(loaded, adder.can_run_list)
+        self._assert_allocatable(tree, adder)
+        self.assertIs(verdict, AddReqResult.NO_TOKEN)
+        # A refused candidate starts no H2D and leaves no lock behind.
+        adder.tree_cache.init_load_back.assert_not_called()
+        self.assertIsNone(loaded.extend_end)
+        self.assertEqual(+tree.locks, Counter())
+        self.assertEqual(
+            tree.swa_evictable_size(),
+            self.WINDOW_DEVICE_SWA + self.OTHER_SWA_EVICTABLE,
+        )
+
+    def test_load_back_admitted_when_swa_covers_its_window_lock(self):
+        tree, adder, loaded, _ = self._admit_batch(swa_available=4000)
+        self.assertIn(loaded, adder.can_run_list)
+        self._assert_allocatable(tree, adder)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(adder.memory_budget.remaining_swa, 0)
+        # Only the request's lock and the in-flight load's lock remain, both on
+        # the loaded node; the admission pins are released.
+        self.assertEqual(+tree.locks, Counter({"best_match": 2}))
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
